hook: A very short file about a batch of hand-labelled cigarettes and the woman their smokers begin to see. Nothing frightening happens on the page; the weight sits in a few lines of handwriting at the very end. Read it slowly and let the last part land on its own.
whyItMatters: SCP-013 is a low-numbered entry that gets by on a single strange effect and a scrap of personal backstory. The anomaly changes nothing in the physical world, only how people see themselves, which makes it a quiet example of the mind-affecting and sensory tags. Its appeal lies less in the mechanics than in the sadness wrapped around them.
thingsToNotice:
Notice how carefully the description pins down the woman's age, height and features while saying nothing about who she was, and how the permanence of the change is stated as a routine detail. That clinical precision makes the missing information louder.

The backstory is delivered flatly: the cigarettes came from the apartment of Irvine Rivers, who killed himself with a massive overdose and was found slumped over his note, surrounded by hundreds of sketches of the same woman. The note is the emotional core. Its tangled grammar shows a man who loves her yet can no longer remember who she was, and the fragment about her favourite flavour hints that the hand-labelled cigarettes were tied to her, so smoking them makes people literally see themselves as the person he lost.
